summary: Priyanka Sharma specializes in Indology. She completed an M.Phil. at Mahatma Gandhi Antarrashtriya Hindi Vishwavidyalaya (2011–2012) and served as an assistant professor at Lovely Professional University from 2018 to 2019.

Priyanku Chakraborty works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Aishwarya Biswas and held positions at The Asiatic Society, including a post in 2022 and the Rajendralal Mitra Research Fellowship in Buddhist Studies attested in 2026.

Priyavrat Sharma (1920–2008) was a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He served as director at Banaras Hindu University, including as director of its Postgraduate Institute of Indian Medicine.

Prods Oktor Skjærvø is a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Oslo, the Sorbonne, and Mainz under Georg Morgenstierne. He worked at Mainz, Columbia, and Harvard, where he was Aga Khan Professor of Iranian Studies (~1991–2015).

Prudence R. Myer (1920–2001) was an art historian working in Indology and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. at NYU's Institute of Fine Arts (~1946–1956) and taught at Mount Holyoke College, Tulane University, and UC Santa Barbara.
Przemysław Szczurek works in the field of Indology. He held a post at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań and was attested in 2021 as Professor of Indology at the University of Breslau.

Puji Sulani is a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history and archaeology. She completed an M.Pd. at the State University of Jakarta (2012–2014), a doctorate at the University of Indonesia (2018–2023), and held a post at STABN Sriwijaya (2009).

Pulinbihari Chakravarti worked in Indology and philosophy, studying under Jogendranath Vedantatirtha and Satkari Mookerjee. He served as Curator of Manuscripts at The Asiatic Society, attested in 1951.
Punyavijaya (1895–1971) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Sukhlal Sanghvi. He founded the Prakrit Text Society.

Purna Harsha Bajracharya is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. In 1972, he was attested as Chief Research Officer at both the Archaeological Survey of India and the Department of Archaeology.

Purnima Dhavan works in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at the University of Michigan and the University of Virginia, she held posts at Bowdoin College and St. John's University before becoming an associate professor of history at the University of Washington (2005).

Purushottam Mahadev Joshi (1904–1989) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held a post at the University of Mumbai Library (~1935–1947) and served as Reader in Medieval History at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1965–1970).

Purushottam Vishvanath Bapat (1894–1991) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Mumbai and Harvard, and held posts at Fergusson College, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Delhi, where he held the chair in Buddhist studies.

Purushottama Bilimoria works in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied under Shivesh Thakur and completed a PhD at La Trobe University. He held academic posts at Deakin University and the University of Melbourne, with visiting appointments at Columbia and Stony Brook.

Pushpendra Kumar (born 1936) is an Indology scholar who studied under Satya Vrat Shastri (~1960–1967). He served as a Sanskrit lecturer at the University of Delhi (~1968–2001) and as principal at Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University.
Puthezhethu Rama Menon (1891–1973) worked in Indology and related fields. He was a retired judge of the Chief Court of Cochin and served as president of the Kerala Sahitya Akademi.
Pyi Phyo Kyaw is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at King's College London in 2014 and later served there as a postdoctoral research fellow (attested 2017).

Pál Büchler (1877–1946) was an Indologist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1897–1907), earning a Ph.D. He later served as a professor at the Commercial School in Târgu-Mureș from 1926 to 1930.

Péter-Dániel Szántó works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and under Alexis Sanderson at Oxford (DPhil 2013). He has held research and faculty posts at Oxford, Hamburg, Leiden, and Eötvös Loránd University.
Qian Cao is an Indology and philosophy scholar. Attested in 2026, they are a PhD student and faculty member at Ghent University.
